newsitem.title: USA: Texas company recalls escargot in bacteria scare.
newsitem.headline: Texas company recalls escargot in bacteria scare.

text.p: A Texas distributor of escargot has ordered a recall of its shipments prior to June 27 because they might be contaminated with bacteria, officials said Monday.

Escargot International Inc, based in Dallas, said the recall was ordered after laboratory tests on its inventory last week found traces of listeria, a bacterium that can cause fever, nausea and stomach aches. It can be fatal in young children or the elderly.

Spokesman Chris Terman said the company believes no more than five pounds of possibly contaminated escargot were still in circulation and that it would be safe if cooked at 165 degrees for just 15 seconds. He said escargot, a type of snail, is usually baked at 400 degrees for about 20 minutes.
"There is not much risk, but if the wrong person ate it with the wrong preparation, it could be a problem," he said, adding that no instances of illnesses have been reported.
The escargot was shipped to restaurants and distributors in about a dozen states. Escargot International handles mainly domestic, rather than imported, escargot, Terman said.
